context: Re-run the severity judgement with reversibility on the table, and record the outcome in the ADR either way. The point is that the record should show reversibility was weighed, not that the answer must change.
description: adr-published-results-history-retention.md, accepted in #1538, chose to retain published-results history rather than rewrite it, on the grounds that the exposed material was private absolute paths of low severity, and explicitly scoped itself not to extend to a higher severity class such as credentials or customer data. That decision was taken without knowing that the pseudonyms which replaced those paths are themselves recoverable by dictionary. Re-mirroring corrects only the branch tip; retained history keeps every superseded value reachable permanently, and a git grep against origin/published-results confirms a token that a candidate value reproduces under the documented transform (measured). The premise needs re-examination - the conclusion may well survive it, but it should survive it explicitly.

preserves.behavior: No recovered plaintext value is written into the ADR, the tracker, or a PR body
Rewriting history on a public branch is never a side effect of another change
The ADR keeps recording what was known at decision time; a re-examination is an amendment with its own date, not a retrofitted rationale
